decisions.question: Which ADRs enter the Decisions section? The phase block names Governed by [ADR-001, ADR-002]. Of its three contracts, topic-model@v1 and topology-ir@v1 name Governed by [ADR-001, ADR-002], and topology-dsl@v2 names [ADR-001, ADR-002, ADR-003]; ADR-003's `affects` frontmatter names topology-dsl@v2 (ADR-001 and ADR-002 name all three contracts).

options.label: ADR-001, ADR-002 and ADR-003
options.consequence: Applies the skill's union rule (the phase's Governed by, each contract's Governed by, every ADR whose `affects` names a contract in the section). The file gains ADR-003's Decision and Consequences (about 55 lines) and a Links line; ADR-003 is accepted, so no 'Not binding until accepted.' line. The topology-dsl@v2 subsection of Contracts cites ADR-003 ten times on six lines, so the plan writer holds the text those citations point to.

options.label: The phase's Governed by only: ADR-001 and ADR-002
options.consequence: Shorter file, but it drops an ADR that a consumed contract is governed by and that `affects` names, leaving ADR-003 cited in the inline contract text with no text of its own, which the skill's selection rule and Rule 2 both exclude. The phase plan, not this step, decides what the phase is governed by.

decisions.why: The skill's Decisions rule is a union, not the phase's list alone, and S105 applied it the same way when the phase block and the contract disagreed (ADR-003 there came from the phase). Here the difference is the direction: the phase block does not list ADR-003 and the consumed contract topology-dsl@v2 does, as does ADR-003's own `affects`. Nothing in the phase's Scope needs ADR-003's rules, but the Contracts section copies topology-dsl@v2's whole Interface and Guarantees, and those cite ADR-003 items. A rule that took the phase's Governed by alone would have changed my mind; the skill's text does not say that.
